title: Cheat-code opcode Trojan in a simple processor decode stage
description: Analyze the RTL source for decode_ctrl, a small instruction-decode control unit, along with its design documentation and documented opcode table. Identify any suspicious or undocumented logic that could allow unauthorized assertion of control signals, and report findings with confidence scores and evidence-based rationale.
constraints: Participants must not modify any file under inputs/.
All analysis output must be delivered as submission/trojan_report.json.
The toolchain (iverilog, vvp, yosys) is optional and available for self-verification only.

candidates.trigger_opcode: string (8-bit hex value or description of triggering condition)
candidates.payload_signal: string (exact RTL net/output name asserted by the payload)

metrics.name: detection_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of ground-truth trojan trigger/payload pairs correctly identified in submitted candidates.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of submitted candidates that reference documented opcodes or unrelated/non-payload signals as trojan findings, relative to total candidates submitted.

metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization
metrics.description: Accuracy of the exact reported opcode value and payload net name against hidden ground truth, scored as exact-match or normalized-equivalent match.

metrics.name: confidence_calibration
metrics.description: Alignment between reported confidence scores and correctness of the finding.

metrics.name: schema_validity
metrics.description: Whether submission/trojan_report.json parses as valid JSON and conforms to the required schema.

interface.timing: Registered outputs, 1-cycle latency, synchronous active-low reset (rst_n) clears all outputs.
